title: Credibility assessment of CFD models for intravascular catheter trackability and flow resistance under ASME V&V 40
runhead: CFD credibility for catheter trackability and resistance
device: Over-the-wire peripheral intravascular catheter (generic family, 4–6 Fr), evaluated for trackability through tortuosity and hydraulic flow resistance

models.name: Model S — Steady-state Navier–Stokes CFD in tortuous vessel with concentric catheter
models.what_it_computes: Annular pressure drop between vessel wall and catheter shaft, tip-region shear and lateral hydrodynamic side-loads under prescribed steady inflow; QOIs include ΔP across the test segment and tip side-load magnitude

models.name: Model T — Transient CFD with prescribed catheter advancement (moving boundary)
models.what_it_computes: Time-resolved axial drag and lateral hydrodynamic side-load on the advancing catheter tip through curvature and stenosis surrogates; QOIs include cycle-averaged ΔP, peak side-load, and integrated hydrodynamic drag during a standardized push

mechanisms.name: M1 — Axial annular pressure-drop governing flow resistance
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Determines delivered flow at set pump conditions and contributes to insertion force budget relevant for design screening

mechanisms.name: M2 — Dean-type secondary flows causing lateral hydrodynamic side-load at bends
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Side-load can bias catheter tracking over a guidewire in tortuous paths and correlates with steering difficulty

mechanisms.name: M3 — Tip and side-port jetting with local recirculation
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Jet-induced asymmetric forces may perturb guidewire alignment and affect trackability near lesions

mechanisms.name: M4 — Hemorheology-dependent viscosity effects
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Non-Newtonian behavior alters both resistance and shear-driven lateral forces across clinically relevant hematocrit

clear_factors: Relevance of the quantities of interest
Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

deviation.detail: All credibility factors are scored on a 0–5 Credibility Index (CI), where 0 = no evidence and 5 = compelling, quantified evidence; CI values are reported for each (model × mechanism) pair in the Results scorecards

sections: Context of use (CoU) and model risk (ASME V&V 40): CoU — Pre-bench design screening to rank catheter variants by predicted trackability surrogates (lateral side-load, drag) and flow resistance (ΔP) for selection into bench testing; Model risk — Medium, because the CFD results inform design gating and test prioritization but do not replace mandatory bench or clinical evidence; consequence of an error is limited to design iteration delays and suboptimal prototype selection, not direct patient harm; model influence is moderate given parallel use of benchtop confirmation
Mechanisms of interest and quantities of interest
Credibility plan and scoring rubric (CI 0–5) mapped to ASME V&V 40 factors
Model inputs — evidence and bounds for each mechanism (Model S and Model T)
Numerical solver error — discretization and iterative error controls for each mechanism (Model S and Model T)
Output comparison — bench loop comparisons and metrics for each mechanism (Model S and Model T)
Relevance of the quantities of interest — linkage to trackability and resistance endpoints for each mechanism (Model S and Model T)
Relevance of validation activities to the CoU — representativeness of test articles and phantoms for each mechanism (Model S and Model T)
Test conditions — alignment with operating envelopes (brief notes per mechanism and model)
Use error — operator-induced variability considerations (brief notes per mechanism and model)
Results: credibility scorecards (CI 0–5) for all (model × mechanism) pairs with concise rationales
Implications for design decisions within the stated CoU
Limitations confined to the assessed factors
